items.title: India's gold imports fall 40% to $24.7 billion in April-October 2026: CTI
items.rss_summary: Gold imports into India declined by around 40 per cent in April-October this year compared to the corresponding period last year, with the country purchasing gold worth USD 24.7 billion during the seven months, Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) Chairman Brijesh Goyal said on Monday. According to Goyal, India imported gold worth USD 41.24 billion between April and October 2025, while the figure stood at USD 24.7 billion during the same period this year, marking a decline of USD 16.46 billion. He said the figures reflected a significant reduction in gold purchases during the current financial year. Gold imports in the 2025-26 financial year stood at around USD 72 billion, while the purchases for 2026-27 are estimated to be between USD 35 billion and USD 40 billion, he said. Goyal attributed the decline in gold purchases to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's appeal, saying the reduction was visible in the trade figures. items.title: Tata Projects bags order for 1,600 MW thermal power plant in Central India
items.rss_summary: EPC major Tata Projects Ltd (TPL) on Monday said it has secured an order to build the complete supporting setup for a 1,600 MW coal-fired power plant in Central India. Under the contract, Tata Projects will be responsible for the design, engineering, manufacture, supply, construction, erection, testing, and commissioning of the project's balance-of-plant systems. These systems encompass critical infrastructure required to support reliable plant operations beyond the boiler-turbine-generator island, the company said in a statement. "Tata Projects Ltd (TPL), one of India's leading Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) companies, has been awarded the complete Balance of Plant (BoP) turnkey package for a 2 x 800 MW ultra-supercritical thermal power project in Central India by a leading integrated power utility," the statement said. items.title: Attero to invest ₹3,000 cr to expand critical mineral extraction capacity
items.rss_summary: E-waste recycling company Attero plans to invest Rs 3,000 crore in the next five years to scale up its critical mineral extraction capacity, a top official of the company said. Attero Co-founder and CEO Nitin Gupta told PTI that the company plans to enhance total e-waste recycling capacity by over four times to 1 million tonnes in the next four years. "We are specifically looking to invest around Rs 3,000 crore in critical minerals facility expansion over the next five years. Roughly 40 per cent of that will go towards lithium, nickel, and if you read the scheme, within nickel, they have said they considered cobalt as well," he said. Attero claims to extract over 22 critical minerals, including gold, silver, copper, aluminum, nickel, lithium, cobalt and rare earths like neodymium, dysprosium, etc. "Our current capacity for electronic waste recycling is around 2,25,000 tonnes per annum.
